title: Heart failure: type, acuity and hypertension
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's heart failure and any related hypertension.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for heart failure and blood pressure management.

HPI
The patient is a 68-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of his chronic heart failure and hypertension. He reports feeling well today and denies any recent shortness of breath, increased swelling in his lower extremities, or significant fatigue. He states that his symptoms have remained stable since his last visit. He continues to monitor his blood pressure at home and reports that readings have been within his target range.

Medication List
Lisinopril 20mg daily
Carvedilol 12.5mg twice daily
Furosemide 40mg daily

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. His skin is warm and dry. Lung sounds are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Heart sounds are regular with no murmurs or gallops noted. Lower extremities show no edema. Blood pressure is 128/78 mmHg and heart rate is 72 bpm.

Assessment
1. Chronic HFpEF: The patient's heart failure with preserved ejection fraction remains stable. His ejection fraction was previously noted at 60%.
2. Hypertension: Blood pressure is well-controlled on current medication.

Plan
Continue current medication regimen. The patient will follow up in three months for a repeat evaluation of his chronic heart failure and HTN.

Electronically signed, K. Nguyen, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: Hypertension with heart failure is presumed linked: I11.0, hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, plus the I50 code.

distractors.why: The classification presumes a causal link between hypertension and heart failure.
The type and acuity are documented: do not use I50.9.
The provider documents diastolic heart failure.
